sources: dossier=asset.md net-position (canonical asset identity uses alias) + intentional-absences (no separate table, compound over claim fields); doc=asset.md invariant 3 (fixed); code=lib/foundation/spec/template.go NodeClaimProducerRef (name/selector/intent/alias/lifetime/data); design-corpus=claim-producer.md (selector, intent, lifetime, scope vocabulary), claim-scope.md (selector)
note: asset.md's rimsky-aware field list (producer/scope/write_semantics) matched neither the code nor the field vocabulary used consistently across sibling concept docs (claim-producer.md, claim-scope.md) and the dossier's own alias terminology. Corroborated across code + multiple design-corpus artifacts, so intent is known without relying on code alone. Fixed invariant 3 to list name/selector/intent/alias/lifetime.

sources: dossier=asset.md net-position bullet 3 ('Committed-durable rows are the asset surface') + required-behaviors ('WHERE state=committed AND lifetime=durable'); doc=asset.md Definition line 11 (fixed) and line 13 (already correct); code=lib/foundation/persistence assets.go and postgres/claim_handles.go filtering state='committed' AND lifetime='durable'
note: The Definition's compound omitted committed state, contradicting the doc's own next sentence, the dossier's explicit required-behavior query shape, and every code filter. Fixed the Definition to name all three conditions (committed, data-processing-capable producer, durable lifetime).

sources: design-corpus=claim-lifetime.md invariant ('Held-durable claim handles persist across instance dispatches' and 'still durable ... just not surfaced as an asset'); doc=asset.md invariant 2 (fixed)
note: asset.md reused 'held-durable claim' for a non-data-processing durable claim, colliding with claim-lifetime.md's distinct use of 'held-durable' for claims persisting across instance dispatches. Corroborated by direct textual comparison of the two concept docs (no dossier entry needed — the collision is self-evident from the design corpus). Reworded asset.md invariant 2 to match claim-lifetime.md's own phrasing and cite it.

sources: design-corpus=child-execution.md ('a thin run-side dispatch helper that ... creates the corresponding child run-scopes and child runs'); doc=run-scope.md invariant (line 36, fixed); code=lib/runtime/child_execution.go DispatchChildren, lib/runtime/fanout_dispatch.go dispatchFanOutChildren (own transaction, separate from sub-claim acquisition)
note: run-scope.md claimed fanout_partition RunScope rows are inserted eagerly in the sub-claim-acquisition transaction; child-execution.md (a sibling concept doc) and the code both attribute creation to the shared dispatch helper's own later transaction. Corroborated across design corpus + code (code corroborates, doesn't solely establish, since child-execution.md already states the same mechanism). Rewrote the invariant to attribute fan-out-partition creation to the dispatch helper's own transaction and cite concept:child-execution instead of a bare invariant id.

sources: dossier=run-scope.md intentional-absences ('Runtime depth-gating safety net — always aspirational ("future capability"), never wired; adjudicated fix-doc: the invariant is reworded enabled-not-built, not implemented now (2026-07-13, transcript; closes the 2026-05-22 artifact promise).') and superseded/historical section; doc=run-scope.md Purpose and invariant (both fixed); code=persistence.RunScopeTable.ListParentChain has zero production callers
note: The dossier explicitly rules this a fix-doc case at transcript tier, directing the invariant be reworded enabled-not-built rather than describing an implemented runtime safety net. Reworded both the Purpose clause and the Invariants entry to state the parent-chain is persisted/queryable but has no runtime caller, and that the canonicalizer's static rejection is the sole enforced defense — respecting the dossier's intentional-absence ruling (no restoration implied).

sources: doc=run-scope.md invariant (line 36, fixed, bare 'per invariant 10' citation removed); design-corpus=run-scope.md's own Invariants section (unnumbered bullets)
note: The bare 'per invariant 10' citation was unresolvable from within the doc (no owning concept named, this doc's own invariants unnumbered) — a self-evident clarity defect independent of the dossier. Resolved as part of the same edit as row 80: the clause was replaced with a concept:child-execution citation instead of a numeral.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy.md required-behaviors ('GET /instances/{id} exposes service_bindings and created_by_api_key_id so the proxy's cache-miss GET-fallback can recover an instance'); doc=host-agent-proxy.md Boundaries (fixed); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy dispatch.go lookupInstance miss -> newControlAPIFetcher
note: The dossier confirms the cache-miss control-API fallback is an intended, corrected mechanism (not a bug), so Boundaries' 'populated via lifecycle-subscriber' was incomplete. Fixed Boundaries to name both the lifecycle-subscriber population path and the cache-miss fallback.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy.md Conflicts needing human ruling, RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (transcript tier): 'executor + claim-producer is the sanctioned late-bind surface ... late-binding a publisher/validation/data-processing service is REJECTED loudly at registration/config ... the 2026-06-08 all-five/no-stubs artifact promise is superseded ... the proxy's server-side handlers for the unreachable three protocols are trimmed per erase-completely'; doc=host-agent-proxy.md invariant (last bullet, fixed); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy publisher_handler.go, validation_handler.go, data_processing_handler.go (still present, not yet trimmed)
note: The narrow finding (invariant 4's failure vocabulary silent on three of five protocols) is actually a symptom of a bigger, transcript-tier-resolved conflict: the doc's protocol-transparency invariant still asserts all five protocols are fronted, but the 2026-07-14 ruling narrowed the sanctioned late-bind surface to executor+claim-producer and rejects the other three at registration. Rewrote the invariant to state the narrowed surface; this also makes invariant 4's 'all dispatch failures' claim accurate again since publisher/validation/data-processing dispatches no longer reach the proxy's dispatch path at all. Code still has the three handlers registered and has NOT been swept to match the 2026-07-14 ruling — that is a separate fix-code item, queued, not touched here.

sources: dossier=host-agent-proxy.md net-position ('The callback_url rewrite to the agent's local_callback_base_url is the ONLY URL the proxy touches', 2026-05-24, artifact; reaffirmed by absence of any later correction through 2026-07-16); doc=host-agent-proxy.md invariant (fixed); code=cmd/rimsky-host-agent-proxy executor_handler.go rewriteCallbackURL (only rewrite site)
note: The trailing clause was forward-looking ('as additional protocols are wired'), barred by the current-state-only rule, and contradicted by the dossier's explicit 'ONLY URL' statement plus the fact that only the callback URL is rewritten today. Removed the clause; invariant now states the callback URL is the only URL rewritten.
